rektion: sich (Dat.) / jdm. etw. (Akk.) verschaffen (einen Überblick, Respekt, Zugang, Klarheit)
meaning_en: to obtain, to get (for oneself or someone); sich einen Überblick verschaffen: to get an overview
definition_de: dafür sorgen, dass man selbst oder jemand anderes etwas bekommt (sich einen Überblick / Respekt / Zugang verschaffen; jdm. eine Stelle verschaffen)
example_de: Gleich am ersten Tag verschafften wir uns vom Kirchturm aus einen Überblick über die Altstadt.
example_en: On the very first day we got an overview of the old town from the church tower.
visual_idea: Collocation 'sich einen Überblick verschaffen' (by far the most frequent use): two tourists at the top of a church tower look down on the whole old town spread out below, so 'Überblick' is literally visible and the dative 'uns' is the people on the tower. Rejected: 'sich Zugang verschaffen' (a person climbing through a window reads as 'einbrechen') and 'sich Respekt verschaffen' (a teacher in a quiet class reads as 'unterrichten').
image_prompt: two young tourists with small backpacks stand at the stone railing of the open gallery at the very top of a tall church tower, one points down at the view; below them a wide panorama of an old German town seen from high above, red tiled roofs, narrow winding lanes, a market square, a river with a stone bridge, green hills on the horizon, clear morning light
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: two young tourists step out onto the gallery at the top of a church tower, walk to the railing and look down at the old town with red roofs, one slowly points across the panorama from the market square to the river; slow pan from the tourists out over the town
